items.question: A pre-registered liquidation study is extended back to 2023-2024. Its 'large liquidation' bar is a per-session p90 of USD liquidation size, ruled on 2025-2026 data. Which threshold applies to which period?

options.label: (a)
options.text: keep the 2025-2026 per-session values for the whole 2023-2026 span

options.label: (b)
options.text: per era: 2023-2024 gets its own per-session p90 pooled over its store; 2025-2026 keeps the ruled values

options.label: (c)
options.text: per half-year per session p90, for all seven half-years (also replaces the ruled 2025-2026 values)

options.label: (d)
options.text: one per-session p90 pooled over 2023-2026, replacing the ruled values

items.rationale: Same rule as the ruled values, applied to each store. Measured: the pooled p90 is 58,630 USD in 2023-2024 vs 60,000 in 2025-2026, so the premise for finer adaptation (USD drift with price) is false; half-year cells swing 2-4x with no price order, so (c) writes local noise into the event definition and changes the already-registered events. (a) ignores the ruling to re-derive per period and puts one session's bar above that era's own p90. (d) replaces the ruled values and is not per period.

items.question: How do two trade stores (2023-2024 and 2025-2026) join in the event scan of a pre-registered study?

options.label: (a)
options.text: one continuous pass across the seam, after a TradeSeq seam check that stops on a gap or duplicate

options.label: (b)
options.text: two independent passes, rolling-window and de-clustering state reset at 2025-01-01

items.rationale: Keeps the 500-trade window and the 30-minute de-clustering correct across midnight; (b) would invent an onset at the seam if a cluster spans it. The seam check guarantees no trade is missing or doubled.
